title: Modernize button variants and iconography; reconcile disabled & loading affordances
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Objective: consolidate button variants (primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost), introduce a first-class IconButton component, and standardize disabled and loading affordances across themes. This ticket reconciles recent token drift (padding/line-height) observed in release runtime-1.18 and fixes regressions that caused visual shifts in toolbars and dense table action rows. Work includes token mapping, updated Figma components, accessible spinner placement for loading states, QA across hosted and dedicated themes, and handoff notes for engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined for all button properties (height, padding, icon spacing, focus ring, border radius) with light/dark/compact theme mappings
IconButton component in Figma with variants: icon-only, icon+label (icon-left, icon-right), small/medium/large, and loading/disabled appearances
Loading affordance preserves button width when spinner is shown (two approaches documented: replace content vs overlay spinner), and preferred approach agreed
Disabled state passes WCAG contrast guidance for text and icon color; focus state suppressed when disabled
Regression visual diff checklist completed for header toolbars, table action columns, and chart control groups with screenshots attached
Design tokens exported and cross-referenced to token names expected by runtime (token map doc link included)
Engineering PR with component code and unit/storybook examples exists and has design approval
implementation_notes: Prefer stable token names to avoid churn: button.height.sm/md/lg, button.padding.sm/md/lg, button.icon-gap

Two loading strategies evaluated: (A) replace content with fixed-width spinner placeholder; (B) overlay spinner with aria-busy. Recommendation: (A) for primary actions to avoid layout shift, (B) for non-critical actions where content must stay visible
IconButton should render as semantic button element with size-only tokens and an aria-label when content is non-textual
Use neutral token aliases for outlines/borders so dedicated themes can override colors without changing layout tokens
Edge case: compact table rows with 28px height require a condensed icon size and negative margin adjustments—add condensed token set
Add visual regression test vector in storybook per variant and theme (light/dark/compact)
